The finale's whole ending, reached only from read_code on a correct code; never returns. Fills both pictures' screen matrices ($0400 and $4400, from $03E8/$43E8 through fill_ptr_bank0/1) with $0E, black ink on light blue paper; switches the VIC to hires bitmap mode (D011 bit 5) with the bitmap at +$2000 (D018 bit 3), light grey border and background; shows the loaded shower picture at $2000 in VIC bank 0 and animates it with black sprites (shapes $0800-$0BBF, pointers $20-$2E) in eight steps separated by delay ($5000); then selects VIC bank 1 to show the cracked-lens picture at $6000, turns every sprite off and stops at $119D. No sound, no keyboard or joystick read; the KERNAL IRQ keeps running.
hires bitmap on; bitmap at +$2000

Step 1: sprites 0 and 1 (shapes $20 at $0800 and $21 at $0840, black, x $91, y $7F and $6B) draw a man's dark head seen from behind beside the woman in the shower; $D015 = $FF turns on all eight sprites, including 2-7 whose pointers and positions this part never set at this point; then delay.

Step 2: the head as four sprites (shapes $22-$25 at $0880-$093F; sprites 0-1 at y $7F, 2-3 at y $6A, all x $90, black), the first frame of the head turning to the left; only sprites 0-3 on ($0F); then delay.
Step 3: the same four sprites with shapes $26-$29 ($0980-$0A3F), the head in profile facing left towards the small machine at the picture's lower left; then delay.

Steps 4 and 5: sprite 4 (black, x $58, y $98, over the top of the small machine at the lower left) shows shape $2A ($0A80), a short horizontal bar, then after a delay shape $2B ($0AC0), a longer bar; $D015 = $1F; delay after each.

Steps 6 to 8: sprite 5 (black) carries a round object with a dotted square on it: shape $2C ($0B00) at x $58, y $98 over the machine, then (INC of the pointer) shape $2D ($0B40) at x $68, y $80, then shape $2E ($0B80, the same image as $2D) at x $78, y $70 with sprite 5 doubled in both directions ($D017 = $D01D = $20), so it flies up and right towards the man's head and grows; a delay after each position.

Last step: makes CIA 2 port A bits 0-1 outputs ($DD02) and writes %10 to them ($DD00), selecting VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF), so the same bitmap mode now shows the cracked-lens picture at $6000 with the matrix at $4400; sprites off ($D015 = 0); then JMP * at $119D forever. Only RESTORE (NMI to finale_start) or a reset leaves it.
the end: loops here for good; RESTORE jumps to $8000 without restoring the VIC

Part entry (the depacker jumps here) and restart point. Points the NMI vector $0318/$0319 at itself, so RESTORE (KERNAL NMI $FE43: SEI, JMP ($0318)) restarts this prompt; SEI (undone by the first CHROUT, which ends in CLI); border, background and background colours 1-2 to black; then prints str_enter_code through KERNAL CHROUT $FFD2 until its $FF terminator and falls into read_code. Reached from the hand-over, from a RETURN-only entry ($808F) and from RESTORE.
PETSCII prompt printed by finale_start, ended by $FF: CLR/HOME ($93), $08 (lock the case switch), cursor down, nine cursor-rights, yellow ($9E), 'PLEASE ENTER CODE', RETURN, cursor down.

Reads the code: up to five characters through KERNAL CHRIN $FFCF (the screen editor returns a typed line after RETURN), skipping zero bytes, storing each in code_input at $8092+Y. A RETURN before the fifth character goes to $808A (flag $1BA0 = 0, back to finale_start). After five characters compares them with secret_code ($809C, 'ILVCT'); a match stores 1 in $1BA0 and jumps to show_ending at $1000. A mismatch ($8078) prints RETURN, cursor up and a space through CHROUT and reads again from here. Characters typed after the fifth are not checked.
all five matched: flag 1, run the ending
wrong code: RETURN, cursor-up, space, then read again
RETURN before five characters: flag 0, restart the prompt (the ending is never reached this way)

Buffer of the characters read by read_code: $8092-$8096 receive up to five characters (a RETURN is stored too when typed early); $8097-$809B are loaded as $FF and never written. The play snapshot holds 'ILVCT' here.
The finale's code, five PETSCII bytes 'ILVCT', compared byte for byte with code_input by read_code. A fixed string in the part, not derived from play.
